Hi Maya — thanks, and great question. High level first, then I'll attach a short sketch.

1) Standard targets (hosted API):
   - p50: typically <= 80ms (application dependent)
   - p95: typically <= 350ms for general-generation requests; heavier generation (long context, streaming) may vary and we document model-specific profiles in the catalog.

2) Measurement windows (how we calculate):
   - Default: 30-day rolling window, daily aggregation into 1-minute buckets, then compute per-bucket percentiles and roll up to p50/p95 for the epoch. This prevents short bursts from dominating while preserving sensitivity to repeated degradation.
   - Alternate option on the table: a 7-day rolling window for customers who want faster feedback.

3) Carveouts and planned maintenance:
   - We allow scheduled maintenance carveouts (must be declared 48h in advance) and will exclude those declared windows from the epoch.
   - For seasonal onboarding/migration (your 72-hr spike), we can offer a single seasonal carveout (up to 96 hours) per 12-month period if scheduled and approved. Emergency cloud outages follow our regional incident carveout policy (incident declared by Redwood Ops).

I've attached a one-page sketch (p50p95_windowing_sketch_v1.pdf) and a matrix with example carveouts (maintenance_carveout_matrix.xlsx). Vivek/Karthik — tagging you for any operational constraints I missed.

Next step: if that wording looks acceptable, I can draft a short clause for procurement/legal to insert into the agreement.

Laura / team — quick operational proposal you can hand to legal/procurement. I kept it short so procurement can paste it into the SOW: 

--- Suggested clause (draft) ---
Measurement and SLOs: Redwood will measure request latency for Hosted API endpoints and report p50 and p95 independently. Measurements will be based on per-minute aggregation buckets computed at the regional edge and reported on a rolling 30-day epoch, unless the parties agree to a 7-day epoch in writing. For each epoch, p50 and p95 will be computed from the distribution of per-request response times observed in non-excluded buckets.

Carveouts: Scheduled maintenance windows will be excluded from the epoch if Redwood provides >=48 hours advance notice. Customer-requested migrations or onboarding events may be excluded if scheduled at least 7 days in advance and approved by Redwood; such seasonal carveouts are limited to a total of 96 hours within any 12-month period. Regional provider incidents declared by Redwood Ops will be handled under incident exclusions and will be communicated via the Redwood status page.

Credits and remediation: If measured p95 for an epoch exceeds the committed target by more than 20%, the parties will trigger a remediation plan as defined in Section X and an SLA credit equal to 5% of that epoch's billable usage for each week the deviation persists, capped at 25% for the affected month.

Operational notes:
- We will provide a per-epoch PDF report containing the per-minute buckets, percentile calculations, and raw sample counts.
- Carveouts will be listed in the report with start/end times and approver id.

--- end draft ---

If this looks OK I'll fine-tune language for legal to avoid circular definitions. Priyom — flag any telemetry limitations or reporting caveats.

—Karthik
